In 1917, this man engaged in a famous debate with Alfred Kroeber on the nature of the superorganic. While at the University of Chicago, he had a notable collaboration with Harry Stack Sullivan, during which he wrote his analysis Navajo Texts. Prior to this he was the chief ethnologist for the Geological Survey of Canada, this led to his methodological work, Time Perspective in Aboriginal American Culture. Other important works include the article "Sound Patterns in Language", and a more famous theoretical collaboration. FTP, identify this author of Language, best known for the linguistic theory he posited with his student Benjamin Wharf.

Along with the labor theory of value, this theory was refuted by Eugen Bohm-Bawerk in his monumental Theory of Capital, while Karl Marx criticized Lassalle's advocacy of the Gotha Programme on account of it. It was initially used in order to criticize the Poor Laws, on the grounds that they would increase the population of labor, which would ultimately lead to more workers, and would both make the workers poorer and rich bankrupt. Assuming that workers are infinitely available, replaceable and interchangeable, this idea built on the work of Malthus. FTP, identify this theory that states that salaries would always converge to subsistence levels, posited by David Ricardo.

When she died of old age Hermes was sent to bring her body to the Elysian Fields. Earlier, her brothers were killed by Comaetho and his Taphian warriors and she refused to marry any man who could not avenge their death. Her future husband accomplished this feat and even though he also accidentally killed her father, Electryon, she consummated her relationship with him. Or so she thought. Actually Zeus had taken the shape of her husband, Amphitryon, and impregnated her. FTP identify this princess of Mycenae who gave birth to the twins Iphicles and Heracles.

The tradition originated with the 84 mahasiddas, and two general types of them exist: the sprul-sku, and the "developed" ones, who have achieved recognition for piety in their lifetime. The state oracle at Nechung is consulted in order to determine the succession of some of them, Of the two most important, one is considered to be the reincarnation of Amitbha, while another is the reincarnation of Avalokiteshvara. One is the traditional head of the Tashilhunpo monastery, while another is the head of the Yellow Hat order, though he has been in exile since 1959. FTP, identify this term for a teacher or leader in Tibetan Buddhism.

In Altruistic Love, he wrote that the study of altruistic love was needed to avert worldwide chaos. He famously distinguished between sensate cultures that were based on empirical science, and ideational cultures based on mysticism. A member of the Kerensky government, he was forced to emigrate after he was sentenced to death by the Bolsheviks, which he wrote about in his autobiography Leaves from a Russian Diary. Following this, he taught at the University of Minnesota until 1930, when he took up his most famous position. FTP, identify this sociologist and author of Social and Cultural Dynamics best known for founding Harvard's sociology department.

As a child he was bathed three times on a summer night and nine times on an autumn night in order to insure that he would be wise. Though he eventually married Kyllikki, her decision to sneak out for a dance confirmed this deity's belief in bachelorhood and romance and he left her to pursue other women in Pohjola. His greatest exploit involved capturing the swan of Tuonela, subsequently being dismembered, but then being restored to life by his sorcerer mom. FTP identify this sworn enemy of Lempo and friend of Vainamoinen, the lovable rake of Finnish myth.

Lesser known works of this philosopher includes Plato's Progress and Dilemmas. He made the distinction between categories and types, arguing that the goal of philosophy is to correct "category mistakes." In his 1922 paper, "Systematically Misleading Expressions" he argued that philosophical problems arise from improper uses of language. In his most famous work, he claimed that all the talk regarding the mental was no more than a certain way of talking about bodies, although he denied that his work was behaviorist. FTP, identify this man who succeeded G.E. Moore as editor of Mind, most famous for his 1949 work, The Concept of Mind.

It begins with a discussion of sensory, secretory, and motor faculties, and subdivides them into further categories like paradoxia and anaesthesia, which are used as case headings in the second part of this work. Many are described without what the author calls "noticeable tain." Number 99 concerns a person who loves only men with mustaches, while number 118 concerns a boy who masturbates only with furs. Consisting of two parts, "General Pathology" and 237 "Case Histories" it often described homosexuality as a deviation. FTP, identify this 1886 work detailing sexual deviants, written by Richard von Krafft-Ebing.

This deity's name curiously means "victory giver," this seems odd because her only son, Narvi, is killed to atone for crimes he did not commit and then his entrails are used as a rope and passed through three slabs of rock to immobilize his father. This successor to Glut and Angr-Boda inadvertently causes earthquakes whenever she goes to dispose of the venom that drips from Skadi's serpent on top of her imprisoned husband's head. FTP identify this long suffering, but steadfast, wife of Loki.

This region's coast is indented by the Gulf of Khambhai (cam-bye) and the Gulf of Kutch; the land between the two gulfs is called the Kathiawar (ca-the-ah-wahr) peninsula. Harappan ruins have been found throughout this state, whose capital, Gandhinagar (gahn-DEE-nah-gahr), lies on the outskirts of Ahmedabad, its largest city. Along with Maharashtra, it became a separate state on May 1, 1960; both states had previously been part of Bombay state. For 10 points - name this western Indian state located between Bombay and the Pakistani border.

One section discusses Kant's confusion of predication with synthesis. This work also presents the example of the Antipodeans, who lack the words to describe their conscious states, in the section "Persons Without Minds." Contrasting the edifying projects of Heidegger, Dewey, and Wittgenstein with more systematic philosophers, this work argues that one should view philosophy as a culturally bound conversation. FTP, identify this work which argues against the metaphor of mind as reflecting the world, written by Richard Rorty.
Philosophy and the Mirror of Nature

This work offers a refutation of reductionism, in that it argues for the primacy of chunking more inclusive concepts instead of breaking things down analytically. Using examples like calculating the area of a parallelogram, this work posits four fundamental mental processes: "reorganization", 'restructuring", "insight", and "understanding." Also using anecdotal examples like Einstein's discovery of relativity, this work demonstrates how one goes from a "bad gestalt" in seeing a problem, to a "good gestalt." FTP, identify this posthumously published work on human creativity, written by Max Wertheimer.

The Trinity Islands, visible off this island's southwest coast, are part of the wildlife refuge that comprises two-thirds of the island. Fort Abercrombie was built on the island during World War II, when its population peaked at about 25,000. Home to the reliquary of the Russian Orthodox saint Herman, its first settlement was founded at Three Saint's Bay in 1794 by Grigory Shelikof, whose namesake strait separates the island from the Alaska Peninsula. For 10 points - name this island, home to a particular species of brown bear.

In one story he was chased from Asterius' court and fled to Asia Minor where he founded Miletus. Another story describes him as the son of Laodameia who ruled Lycia and helped his brother Priam during the Trojan War. In a memorable scene from the Iliad, Apollo anointed him with ambrosia and cleaned his body after he was killed by Patroclus causing his father, Zeus, to weep for him. FTP identify this brother of Minos and Europa.

An opponent of Frederic Bartlett, this man's namesake illusion consists of a circle surrounded by larger circles, which appears larger than the same circle flanked by smaller circles. He tried to apply Fechner's theories to higher mental processes in works like The Intelligence of Schoolchildren and he wrote a treatise on color vision based on a double pyramid. He is best known, however,for his innovations in psychological experimentation, discovering the serial position curve, and devising the word completion test. FTP, identify this psychologist, best known for his work On Memory.

The definition of this concept was called into question by Edmund Gettier, who attacked the established doctrine that had dated back to Plato's Theaetetus. Externalists argue that it is possible to possess it unawares, while internalists deem it a matter of the correct relation of ideas in the mind. Foundationalists claim that one must have correct basic beliefs to possess it, while coherentists argue that it is a matter of the interlocking of beliefs. FTP, identify this concept which, according to Cartesian skepticism, humans entirely lack.

His poetic works in Punjabi include the Chandi Di Var, which concerns a contest between the gods and demons. His sons Zorawar and Fateh were betrayed to the faujdar of Sirhind, who had them executed. Opposing the Mughals, he was assassinated at Nanded in 1708. Known for organizing the Khalsa as well as transferring the line of succession to the Adi Granth, he rose to power after his father, Teg Bahadur was murdered. FTP identify this 10th and last Guru of Sikhism.

Her totem symbol is simply a solid stone pillar, which represents her role as a foundation of order. She was called the "Daughter of Ra," and pharaohs often referred to themselves as her "beloved" in order to show their commitment to justice. Depicted as a tall, winged woman, she had a namesake hall, where Anubis determined whether souls would enter the Fields of Peace or be devoured by the jaws of Ammut, using her as the source of judgment. FTP, name this Egyptian goddess of truth, whose feather was weighed against the hearts of the dead to determine their fate.

Several of them have had the suffix "-natha," or "lord," appended to their name as an additional sign of respect. Because they are believed to be alike, they are all identified by colored emblems that were associated with their entry into the world. Their name is derived from their metaphorical role of making a path for others to follow while fording across the river of life's endless cycle of rebirths; and the nineteenth, Malli, was believed to be a woman according to the Svetambaras. FTP, name this Jainist term for a person who has become immortal through enlightenment, twenty four of whom have existed.

He argued that the market economy functions because of constraints that exist outside the market in his Legitimation Crisis. He also argued for a scaled version of Kant's moral philosophy called discourse ethics. He expounded on the dual nature of laws in democracies in Between Facts and Norms, and attacked revisionists who tried to trivialize Nazism in The New Conservativism. Known for his debates with Hans-Georg Gadamer, this author of The Structural Transformation of the Public Sphere was a student of Max Horkheimer and Theodor Adorno. FTP, name this philosopher who wrote The Theory of Communicative Action.

The author of Eisenhower's statement that "freedom means the freedom to fail as well as to succeed", this social theorist was also a pioneer in the field of medical sociology. His educational theories centered on role allocations, while he posited that Ascription and Achievement were the two poles on his Axis of Social Stratification. The author of Family, Socialization, and the Interaction Process, and The Social System, in his best known work he discussed the Unit Act of Social Systems. FTP, identify this sociologist, best known for The Structure of Social Action.

Luke 21:31 is used as proof of this idea, as is Matthew 16:18, where Jesus puns on the word kepha, or rock, to describe the church. Its most notable opponent was Joseph Strossmayer, Bishop of Diakovar, whose speech against it was famously praised by Pius IX. It is considered a nontransferable charisma, and to employ it, the doctrine must have an associated consequence if not agreed with, it must be taught in public, and it must apply to the entire Church. Most famously invoked by Pius XII concerning Mary's Assumption, this is FTP, what doctrine, which holds that when a statement is made ex cathedra, the pope cannot be wrong?

First described concretely by Robert Torrens in Essay on the External Corn Trade, one famous argument against it is the "infant industry" argument. When it is not being followed, the world is not operating on its PPC. Classically, it assumes that labor is the only input, that goods are homogenous across firms, and that transportation costs are negligible, meaning that it is profitable to export. With two or more countries, free trade then proceeds until the prices of exports are equal across countries. Frequently illustrated with the example of English cloth and Portuguese wine this is, FTP, what theory which states that countries should produce and export those goods which for them have the lowest opportunity costs.

In one of his works, this philosopher distinguished between verbal and real propositions, while espousing his doctrine of enumerative induction. He defended Richard Carlile in a series of famous letters to the Chronicle, while his series of articles on "The Spirit of the Age" appeared in The Examiner in 1830. Some of his political work was compiled into Considerations on Representative Government, while his reading of Richard Whately led to his System of Logic. His political liberalism culminated in his Subjection of Women. FTP, identify this philosopher, the author of On Liberty and Utilitarianism.

He mentions that his brother is Meili, and is taunted for hiding in the thumb of a glove, afraid to sneeze or fart for fear of Fjalar, in "The Lay of Harbard." The giantess Grid gives him an unbreakable staff and a pair of iron gloves during his quest to kill Gerrod, as well as Megingjarpar, his girdle. This father of Magni and Modi has to dress up as Freya to kill Thrym and recover his most prized possession, which was made by Brok and Eitri. FTP name this husband of Sif and son of Jord and Odin, the Norse god of thunder and lightning.

His work has recently been reintroduced into the field of modern organizational theory by Oliver Williamson. One of his works investigates the incentives involved in entrepreneurship, ignoring the advantage of non contractual relationships. The founder of the field of "New Institutional Economics", his did much of his early work on monopolies He identified the importance of transaction costs in "The Nature of the Firm", but he is better remembered for the ideas on property rights he espoused in "The Problem of Social Costs." FTP, identify this winner of the 1991 Nobel Prize, best known for his eponymous theorem.

Bellerophon's cousin, many myths name him as the ruler of Tyrins. This son of Idomene and Amythaon attempts to steal King Phylacus' cattle, to give his brother Bias as a wedding gift, result in his imprisonment. Earlier he had been out with Polyphantes when his decision to spare a nest of snakes resulted in a remarkable transformation. In jail he proves his abilities by predicting that the roof of the cell will cave in the next morning. Later on he treats Iphiclus' mysterious impotence after learning that the latter had been terrified of his father's gelding knife as a boy. He is clued into these events by listening to worms and vultures respectively. FTP identify this Greek seer who understood the languages of beast and birds.

This work plays a key role in Derrida's Dissemination, particularly in his discussion of the pharmacy. This dialogue is set under a plane-tree, by the banks of the Ilissus. Its only two speakers are Socrates and the titular character, who is returning from visiting Lysias. Their discussion of Eros leads into Socrates' description of the two sometime-dueling desires, that for pleasure and that for the best. This in turn leads to Socrates' monologue which includes the notable metaphor of the soul as a charioteer and horses. FTP, name this Platonic dialogue that ends with the ostensible conclusion that writing is inferior to speech.

His last major book was a set of "reflections on liberty, society, and government," Dominations and Powers. He wrote about Lucretius, Dante, and Goethe in Three Philosophical Poets and divided reality into the four realms of matter, spirit, truth, and essence in his magnum opus. His literary work includes a novel about Oliver Alden, The Last Puritan. For 10 points - name this American philosopher of The Life of Reason and Scepticism and Animal Faith, who accused those who forget history of being condemned to repeat it.

In a poem by C. K. Williams, this man appears reincarnated as a fly. He examined the way commercials help define our concept of "masculine" and "feminine behavior" in the work Gender Advertisements. His essays "Where the Action Is" and "On Face-Work" appear in Interaction Ritual, which followed his Behavior in Public Places. In a more interesting tale, he spent months in mental institutions in order to write Asylums. For 10 points - name this sociologist who wrote Stigma and The Presentation of Self in Everyday Life.

He suggested that one could make the most of chances through self-development in his 1982 article "The Psychology of Chance Encounters in Life Paths." Much of his work dealt with social learning and aggression, and included a 1959 collaboration with Richard Walters, Adolescent Aggression, and his most famous experiments in this field involved, showing children film of a woman acting violently and observing their behavior when placed in identical surroundings. FTP, name this psychologist whose Bobo doll experiments investigated his concept of reciprocal determinism.

Eight of the ten books of the Rig Veda begin with dedications to this god. A Brahmana text states that Yama gave this god his immortality, but in the Rig Veda, Yama merely tells Varuna that he is hiding in the waters. This son of Aditi and Kasyapa rescues Hanuman from Ravanna's wrath in the Ramayana and in the Mahabarata, it is he rather than Shiva who begets Skanda with his wife Svaha. But the most important role of this two faced god is that of messenger to the gods and bearer of sacrifices. FTP, identify this figure, whose face is often smeared with butter, the Hindu god of fire.

Its author used William Jones as a source in his claims that virtue and holiness does not proceed from reflection. According to this work, all objects of perception must follow a four form principle: the physical form, the mathematical form, the logical form, and the moral form. Reality is an object in the mind of the subject, a perception of the perceiver. Reality is also determined by will, which is not governed by the principle of sufficient reason. FTP, these concepts are purported in what book which dichotomizes reality by Arthur Schopenhaur?
The World As Will and Idea

Al Jissah and Al Sifa are among this coastal city's beaches, while one may visit the Wadi Sireen Nature Reserve in the district of Al Amerat. The Muttrah wilayat is home to its new port, Mina Qaboos, named for the sultan who modernized it, while the wilayat of Seeb is home to famous bull races as well as the city's international airport. The forts of Al Jalali and Al Mirani are the most prominent landmarks in, FTP, what city, Oman's capital?

Complexity theorists oppose this philosophical idea, while Douglas Hofstadter's problems with it form a main component of G?del, Escher, Bach. Daniel Dennett claims that a "greedy" version of this concept exists when those using it try to explain too much with too little. The linguistic version of it claims that everything can be described in a language with a limited number of core concepts, while the methodological type states that explanations of things should be pared down to the simplest entities possible. For 10 points - identify this idea that generally states that complex things can be explained in terms of their constituent components, the opposite of holism.

The people quoted in it are known as the Tanna'im, while many of its contributors were centered at Yavneh. Unique in it is the Pirke Avot, a collection of moral sayings, which lacks the traditional commentary that accompanies it other parts. It includes the Nezkim, which concerns laws dealing with civil and criminal matters, the Zeraim, which pertains to agriculture, the Nashim, which describes laws regarding vows, the Kodashim, which relates to ritual slaughter, and the Tohorot, which concerns ceremonial purity. Compiled by Rabbi Judah the Prince, identify - for 10 points - this Jewish collection of oral law, whose commentary is known as the Gemara.

Georgescu-Roegen criticized this as merely being an exercise in math, citing as an example a paper that assumed more traders than there are real numbers. The Sonnenschein-Mantel-Debreu theorem states that demand functions in these models can have arbitrary shapes. Arrow and Debreu introduced the modern "neo-Walrasian" ideas of how to build them. These models posit that every goods market is embedded in a larger economy and so the supply and demand curves affect each other. For 10 points - identify this branch of microeconomics concerned with determining levels of production, consumption, and prices for all commodities in an economy simultaneously.

Worship of him was centered in Lampsacus, and he was depicted as carrying a pruning knife, as he is the deity of gardening and doubles as a scarecrow. He attempted to rape the nymph Lotis, whom Zeus promptly changed into the lotus tree. He also tried to violate Hestia at a rustic feast while all the other gods slept, but, in symbolic disapproval of such an inhospitable act, an ass brayed and awoke Hestia before this minor deity could get to her. Fathered by either Adonis or Dionysus on Aphrodite, name - for 10 points - this minor deity known for the impressive proportions of his phallus.

The recently discovered Ravi phase pushes its history back to 3300 BCE, long before the previously known Kot Diji Phase. Using four-to-five-character-long inscriptions on seals, this people's language has been tentatively identified as Dravidian. Akkadian references to "Meluhha" and "Makkan" give evidence of their foreign trade. Probably reaching from Sutkagen Dor near the Arabian Sea to Rupar in the Simla Hills, its main cities were located in present-day Pakistan. For 10 points - name this civilization, whose two major cities were Mohenjo-daro and Harappa, and which is named for the river valley system in which it is located.

On one of his journeys this father of Falka and Rispa is nearly abducted by the sorcerer Rossthiof. His abilities, some which he shares with Hofvarpnir, allow him to defeat Gullfaxi after a rash wager is made with Hrungnir. He may symbolize the bearers of a coffin, since he once undertook a journey to Helheim with Hermod, though he is usually an emblem of time, as he was conceived as part of a ploy to prevent Blast from meeting a six-month deadline in completing the wall around Asgard, when Loki seduced his father Svadilfari while disguised as a mare. FTP, name this eight-legged steed of Odin.

In this work, the contrast between the Einverseeling and Einverleibung is brought to bear on the right to make promises that distinguishes its two classes. The evolution of punishment from a means to collect debt is discussed in its second essay, while its third relates the role of the orgy of feeling introduced by the ascetic priest that leads to a sick will. The title concept is presented as a product of resentment of the blonde beast, or the masters, by the slaves, and it ends with the statement "man would rather will nothingness than not will." FTP, name this work written as a supplement to Beyond Good and Evil, by Friedrich Nietzsche.

Minority ethnic groups of this country include the Parya and Yazgulam. Its Great Gissar Canal is an irrigation project that attempts to reclaim parts of the Zeravshan and Vakhsh valleys. Its eastern region contains the city of Khorugh, the capital of its autonomous Badakhstan region, while Khujand occupies a northern reach of this country that extends into the Fergana Valley. Most of its citizens speak a dialect of Farsi. FTP, name this country, home to peaks like Lenin Peak and Communism Peak, located in the western Pamir Mountains whose capital is at Dushanbe.

The Patristic and Protestant "Idea" of this figure were the subject of two essays by Cardinal Newman. In the French Jour du Judgement his parents are given as Angingnars and a woman of the Babylonian tribe of Dan. Frederick II was a popular Medieval candidate for him and Hus and Wyclife associated him with the Pope. Although he is only definitively mentioned in the letters of John, many associate him with "the man of sin" in Paul's 2nd Thessalonians or the beast "with seven heads and ten horns" of Revelation. For 10 points - identify this figure from Christian mythology, a false messiah who will precede the Second Coming.

Josiah Royce developed a "pragmatic" or "voluntaristic" variety of this philosophical theory which appealed to a collection of persons infusing the world with purpose. Fichte opposed it to dogmatism and created a version of it based upon the transcendental ego. Plato's theory of the Forms is an ancient example of it, while Hegel created an "Absolute" version of it. It is stated as "esse est percipi" or "to be is to be perceived" in its most famous formulation, by George Berkeley. For 10 points - identify this philosophical theory, opposed to materialism, which contends that the external world is dependent on the mind.

In Book III of the Aeneid Aeneas relates that she gave a Phrygian scarf and gold embroidered robes to Ascanius. One of her sons founded Pergamum naming it after himself while another, Molossus, was the founder of a royal dynasty in Epirus. She is saved by Peleus from the machinations of Hermione and Menelaus as the title character of a Euripidean drama. Her final husband is Helenus although she had become the concubine of Neoptolemus after the Trojan War. During that conflict her father, Eetion, and seven brothers were all killed by Achilles and after it her son Astyanax was thrown from the walls of Troy. For 10 points - name this wife of Hector.

Notable translators of it include Alexander Heidel, who rendered all the dirty passages into Latin, and John Gardner. The characters include Siduri "whose drinks refresh the soul" and Ninsun the title character's mother, who interprets many of this dreams. Often known by its first line "He who saw everything," in the latter part of the work the hero encounters talking scorpions who allow him to ascend Mount Mashu and a snake who steals the plant of eternal life which Utnapishtam had told him of. Earlier the hero slew Humbaba and the Bull of Heaven with his friend Enkidu. For 10 points - identify this Babylonian poem about a king of Uruk.

The earliest one lived at Marpessus, while the one from Erythrae revealed to Alexander the Great his divine descent. The most famous one accompanied Aeneas into the underworld and showed him how to pluck the Golden Bough, having earlier gained a thousand years of life for becoming Apollo's lover without thinking to ask not to age. Named Deiphobe, she sold Tarquinius Superbus three of her books of prophecies, having burned the other six when he refused her initial price. For 10 points - who were these prophetesses of Apollo, the most famous of which was the Cumaean one?

By crushing Osgar's shield with his spear he revealed the location of the cave to which he had retreated after killing Cairell at the Battle of the White Strand, leading to his death and the desire for revenge by his brother Conan. Although he was already married to Scandlach, he was offered the hand of Cainche to cement his reconciliation with his greatest enemy, whose enmity he gained in the Battle of Cnucha, where he killed Cumhal. For 10 points - who was this enemy of Finn Mac Cool, the leader of the Morna clan?

This city's suburbs include Carlton, Collingwood, Richmond, Prahran, St. Kilda, and Brighton, and it is home to Monash and LaTrobe Universities. Permanent settlement in the area began in 1835, when John Batman made a treaty with local inhabitants. The city grew dramatically i? The 1850s after gold was found in nearby Bendigo and Ballarat. The Yarra River meets Port Philip Bay at -- for 10 points -- what city that served as Australia's capital before Canberra was founded and is named after Queen Victoria's first Prime Minister?

This philosopher's studies of indirect self-reference inspired and eponymous computer program that outputs its own source code. He argued that scientific theories are confirmed or disconfirmed as a whole, and that epistemology needs to be naturalized. With Pierre Duhem he advocated ontological relativity, and he argued for the indeterminacy of translation in Word and Object. Other important works include From a Logical Point of View and The Roots of Reference, but he is best known for attacking the analytic - synthetic distinction. For 10 points -- identify this author of "Two Dogmas of Empiricism."

In antiquity, some people thought he had turned into the constellation The Charioteer, presumably because of the way he died. Some myths have him being restored to life by Aesclepius and transported to Italy to become an attendant to Artemis, the goddess with whom he shares the final scene of Euripides' play named for him. That play is Euripides' second of the same name: the first is lost, but originally failed because of its shocking portrayal of the female lead as sexually aggressive. For 10 points -- name this son of Theseus whose persistently virginity annoyed Aphrodite so much that she made his stepmother Phaedra fall in love with him.

Known as Fintan in some legends, this mythological figure was renowned for imbibing crimson hazel nuts. The poet Finneces spent seven years in search of it, which was said to dwell in the well of Seagis near the river Boyne, because it had been prophesized that its captor would be rewarded with omnipotence. Eventually caught with the aid of the youth Demne, the youth burnt his finger preparing it and when he sucked on his thumb to cool the burn became beneficiary of its gift. Described in the Fenian cycle --for 10 points -- name this mythical creature responsible for the wisdom of Fionn MacCool.

The Benini coefficient is a surface description of patterns of this phenomenon whose occurance the Featherman-Jones-Hauser hypothesis attempts to explain. The Blau-Duncan model was previously used an example of it within the status-attainment tradition. Durkheim claimed that a high vertical rate of it would lead to individual and society anomie, while the earliest theory for it may be Vilfredo Pareto's circulation of elites. FTP, name this sociological term which refers to the shifting within a system of social stratification.

Extending from the Lesser Caucasus to the margin of the Kura River lowland, the early nineteenth century saw the dissolution of the namesake khanate and in the Treaty of Gulistan this region passed to Russia. Its parliament declared its independence in 1991, though it is only recognized by Yerevan. Reaching its maximum height at Gyamysh, its chief industrial center and capital is Stepanakert. FTP name this enclave of the Caucasus, claimed by both Armenia and Azerbaijan.

His studies under Natorp influenced his first book, 1931's Plato's Dialectical Ethics. He argued with Derrida in his 1989 work Dialogue and Deconstruction, and also with Habermas, who criticized this man's rejection of the Enlightenment's "prejudice against prejudice." However, it was his debates with his teacher Heidegger that influenced his most famous work, which uses the beautiful in art as an analogy to the way a text draws its readers into the event of truth by making claims on them. FTP, identify this German philosopher and proponent of hermeneutics, the author of 1960's Truth and Method.

The author of this text received criticism for his erroneous description of pottery in advanced civilizations. Annotated and used as a source by Marx, this work's chapters are named after its central classification scheme's parts, which are outlined in the first chapter, "Ethnical Periods." This work centers on elements of social structure such as "Arts of Subsistence" and "Systems of Consanguinity". This work divides communities into savagery, barbarism, and civilization, all based on its author's studies of the tribes of the Iroquois League. FTP, identify this anthropological work by Lewis Henry Morgan.

Its name means "addition" and it exists in two forms: the Bavli and the Yerushalmi. Composed by the Amora'im between the 3rd and 5th centuries, some of this religious text's contributors include Rav Ashi and Rav Papa, though the most famous might be Rabbi Judah, known as the redactor of the text upon which this work is based. This work covers thirty-six and a half of the sixty tractates that comprise the work upon which it is based, including the orders regarding Sabbath, family law, and Temple worship. FTP, identify this Jewish text that is part of the Talmud and a commentary on the Mishnah.

The original introduction to this work described it as a "pamphlet" which the author wrote in his spare time. Chapters in this seminal text include "The 'Inevitability' of Planning" and "Economic Control and Totalitarianism". Towards the end, this work discusses the fall of Nazism and totalitarian regimes, and earlier extols the virtues of democracy, which promotes laissez-faire economic policy. Its first and most famous chapter, "The Abandoned Road", discusses the failure of socialism in the modern world. FTP, identify this most famous work of Friedrich von Hayek.

While born in Clazomenae, this philosopher became the first pre-Socratic to teach in Athens and gained the patronage of Pericles, who helped him with an acquittal after being charged with impiety. Like every other pre-Socratic, he wrote an On Nature in which he postulated that the universe was composed of an infinite number of primordia in conscientious objection to Empedocles. His cosmogony was based on the idea of the good mind, or nous. FTP, identify this Greek philosopher who was a close adherent to the philosophy of Anaximenes.
